- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., > +2.0 in 3-day window), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overhang.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed — increase initial forecast by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model may prematurely assume continuation; instead, allow 1–2 days of “stagnation” before reversing.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., > +1.5) correlate with model underestimating upside — increase forecast by 2–3% for 3–5 days following sentiment surge.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 2–3 days, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature reaction.
- In low-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment < 0.0 for 5+ days), model often underestimates downside risk — add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for hidden volatility.
